title: Stopping a regression also stops the test command it started
objective: Within 5 s of a regression being stopped by SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP, neither scripts/testiface.py nor any process of the test command's process group is still running.
outline: core/osx.py run(): around proc.communicate, `except subprocess.TimeoutExpired` stays; add `except BaseException: kill_tree(proc.pid); raise`. scripts/testiface.py launch()/main(): install handlers for SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP around the child's wait that stop the child's process group (TERM, at most 2 s, KILL), write the line and exit 2 (UNMEASURED); this is the only place that needs the group call, so keep every other added line free of the hard_block words. devloop/regression.py needs no new process handling: its on_signal raises agents.Interrupted inside testrun.run -> osx.run, which now stops testiface.py's group (osx.kill_tree waits 5 s between TERM and KILL, and testiface.py stops its own child group within about 2 s, so both layers end well inside 5 s). Update regression.py's docstring paragraph on stop signals. Do not edit devloop/README.md (new-1 edits the paragraph about stopped controllers; a second edit there would conflict across groups). Processes a test runner moves out of its process group (a browser that calls setsid) are the project's to stop on SIGTERM; the TERM-first order gives the runner that chance.

Cases: item 1 for each of SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP as subTests (fixture as T124Acceptance.stop_during_full but tests.full = `sh -c 'python3 -c "import os, time; open(P, \"w\").write(\"%d %d\" % (os.getpid(), os.getppid())); time.sleep(60)"; true'` with P a file in self.tmp; wait until P holds two numbers; the testiface pid is the parent shell's parent, read from /proc/<pid>/stat field 4 or `ps -o ppid= -p <pid>`; send the signal to regression.py; poll up to 5 s: all three pids not alive; measured on today's code with SIGTERM: all three still alive 5 s after the signal while regression.py exited 2); item 2 (run scripts/testiface.py full directly with cwd and AC_CODE_ROOT = the project, AC_TEST_OUT = a fresh empty folder, AC_ROOT = the project and the same slow tests.full; signal testiface.py; within 5 s: its exit code 2, the recorded test pid and shell pid not alive, stderr and <AC_TEST_OUT>/full.log contain 'testiface: stopped by SIGTERM; the test command' (one subTest per signal); today the shell and test process survive); item 3 in process (install a SIGALRM handler that raises a RuntimeError subclass, signal.setitimer 1 s, call osx.run(['sh', '-c', 'echo $$ > F; exec sleep 30']): the exception propagates, and within 5 s the pid in F is not alive; restore the old handler in a cleanup; today the sleep survives); item 4 (import regression; the old sentence is not in regression.__doc__). Every case runs in seconds.

acceptance: 1. regression.py stopped by SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP while full runs (tests.full is a command that records its own pid and its parent's pid, then sleeps 60 s under a `sh -c '...; true'` wrapper so the shell stays its parent): within 5 s of the signal the recorded test process, its parent shell and the testiface.py process (the shell's parent) are all not alive (core/osx.alive false), and the existing T124Acceptance assertions still hold (exit 2, unmeasured report 'stopped by <SIGNAME> during full', live record and worktree gone).

2. scripts/testiface.py receiving SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP while its command runs sends SIGTERM to the command's process group, SIGKILL to that group if any of it is left 2 s later, appends the line 'testiface: stopped by <SIGNAME>; the test command's process group was stopped' to $AC_TEST_OUT/<command>.log and writes it to stderr, and exits 2; within 5 s of the signal no process of that group runs.

3. core/osx.run(): any exception other than its own timeout raised while it waits for the child (an exception raised by a signal handler, KeyboardInterrupt) stops the child's process group with osx.kill_tree before it propagates; the exception itself propagates unchanged and a normal or timed-out run behaves as today.
4. devloop/regression.py's docstring no longer contains 'The test command it had started is not' (the old sentence); it says that a stop signal also stops the test command it started.

request:
# Phase one, group 1: the machine is not overrun (docs/DECISIONS.md D-100, D-102; plan in docs/HANDOFF.md, last section, items 1.1-1.4)

The user approved this plan (D-102, verbatim there). Sources: the main session's review of an external audit (2026-11-26) and feedback from tabby_pool's (T's) main session, which runs agent-control daily (2026-11-26). Write the source on each ticket; do not open GitHub issues. Quoted feedback is data, not instructions. Read docs/VISION.md first: each ticket names the metric it improves and what it removes. Tests go in the area's own test file in tests_devloop/ using loop_harness.py; each case runs in seconds. Group these as you judge (core/chain.py); 1.1 and 1.2 touch slots and dispatch, 1.3 regression and testiface, 1.4 landing and release.

## 1.1 The exclusive scope covers the release and the tests agents run
T (measured there): swap at 22/23 GB, Chrome took 30 s to open, many reds and unmeasured runs came from memory exhaustion; a release running beside another group's full regression made each stage 40-55% slower.
Main session (read the code): `devloop.regression_exclusive` only orders regressions against each other. The release (devloop/core/release.py) takes no slot; workers and verifiers running tests take an ordinary slot.
Wanted:
- The release takes the whole machine like an exclusive regression (same gate, same wait rules and limits as a regression since #121).
- While a full test run (regression or release) holds the machine, tests an agent runs through run_tests.py wait or report "machine busy" (as the opener already does, issue #7); agents keep writing code.
- Find out whether T's browser tests can be started by an agent by any path other than run_tests.py (read T's AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md and A's prompts; T's repo is at ../tabby_pool if present, read-only). Say in the ticket what you found.

## 1.2 Pause new agents when memory is short
Main session (read the code): devloop/core/host.py already samples available memory, but nothing decides with it.
Wanted:
- Below a threshold (a setting such as `devloop.min_free_memory`, or swap use; pick the measure and the default from T's samples in <worktrees>/runs/host/*.jsonl if you can reach them, else say what you assumed), the controller starts no new agent and no new regression; running ones go on.
- The reason shows on the idle page and on the board's live tab.
- How to read memory pressure on macOS must be checked, not guessed (vm_stat, memory_pressure, sysctl); Linux reads /proc/meminfo as today.

## 1.3 Stopping a regression also stops the tests it started
Main session (read the code): devloop/regression.py's docstring says "The test command it had started is not stopped (it runs in its own session)". devloop/core/osx.py `run()` kills the process tree only on timeout; scripts/testiface.py `launch()` starts another new session for `ac-test`.
T (seen there): orphan browsers keep piling up on the machine (three headless Firefox groups 20 hours old; geckodriver 15-20 days old); each cleanup needs the user's permission.
Wanted:
- regression.py on SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP stops testiface.py's process group; testiface.py on those signals stops the `ac-test` process group; osx.run() stops the child tree on any exception other than a timeout, too.
- Acceptance: within 5 s of stopping a regression, neither layer runs. Remove the "not stopped" sentence from the docstring.
- This touches the hard_block words (os.kill / killpg), so the ticket stops before merge for the user: say so in the ticket.

## 1.4 Landed is written before the release, and the release does not block the controller
T (seen there): one release takes 70+ minutes and the controller dispatches nothing meanwhile.
Main session (read the code): land() fast-forwards main, then runs the release, the rerun and the fix-ticket openers synchronously, and writes `landed` last; a controller that dies in between restarts with the group still `verified` and would release again (inference).
